Lessons.Title: Introducing Polynomials
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Identify relative minimums and relative maximums of graphs of polynomials. Identify the degree, leading term, and constant term of a polynomial.

A polynomial is a finite sum of nonnegative integer powers with real coefficients. The degree is the largest exponent of a nonzero term, the leading term has that degree, and the constant is the x-independent term. A graph may have relative maxima or minima that require examining turning behaviour, not just counting terms.

Source activity 3.1: Which One Doesn’t Belong: What are Polynomials?: Which one doesn’t belong? A: \(4 - x^2 + x^3 - 4x\) B: \(2x^4 + x^2 - 5.7x + 2\) C: \(x^2 + 7x - x^{\frac13} + 2\) D: \(x^5 + 8.36 x^3 - 2.4 x^2 + 0.32x\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 3.2: Card Sort: Equations and Graphs: Your teacher will give you a set of cards. Group them into pairs that represent the same polynomial function. Be prepared to explain your reasoning. Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 3.3: Let’s Make Some Curves: Use graphing technology to write equations for polynomial functions whose graphs have the characteristics listed when plotted on the coordinate plane. A 1st degree polynomial function whose graph intercepts the vertical axis at 8. A 2nd degree polynomial function whose graph has only positive \(y\)-values. A 2nd degree polynomial function whose graph contains the point… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: Select all points where relative minimum values occur on this graph of a polynomial function. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: Add one term to the polynomial expression \(14x^{19}-9x^{15}+11x^4+5x^2+3\) to make it into a 22nd degree polynomial. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Identify the degree, leading coefficient, and constant value of each of the following polynomials: \(f(x)=x^3 - 8 x^2 - x + 8\) \(h(x)=2 x^4 + x^3 - 3 x^2 - x + 1\) \(g(x)=13.2 x^3+3 x^4 - x - 4.4\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: We want to make an open-top box by cutting out corners of a square piece of cardboard and folding up the sides. The cardboard is a 9 inch by 9 inch square. The volume \(V(x)\) in cubic inches of the open-top box is a function of the side length \(x\) in inches of the square cutouts. Write an expression for \(V(x)\).… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: Consider the polynomial function \(p\) given by \(p(x)=7x^3 - 2x^2 + 3x+10\). Evaluate the function at \(x=\text-3\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: An open-top box is formed by cutting squares out of an 11 inch by 17 inch piece of paper and then folding up the sides. The volume \(V(x)\) in cubic inches of this type of open-top box is a function of the side length \(x\) in inches of the square cutouts and can be given by \(V(x)=(17-2x)(11-2x)(x)\). Rewrite this… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Edulytics independent cool-down: Find the degree, leading coefficient and constant of -2x^3+5x-9. Expected reasoning or answer: Degree 3, leading coefficient -2, constant -9.
